errors.not_authorized: This target is not marked as authorized: only websites and code we own or have written permission for are scanned.
errors.dns: The domain «{host}» could not be found.
errors.private_ip: «{host}» points to an internal address ({ip}). To scan the internal network, enable 'allow_private' in the configuration.
errors.redirect_away: The website redirects to another domain ({url}). Create a target for that domain if it is also yours.
errors.no_dir: The folder «{path}» does not exist on the server.
errors.dir_not_allowed: The folder «{path}» is not inside the allowed folders ('code_roots' in the configuration).
errors.no_source: This code target has neither a folder nor a .zip file.
errors.no_zip_ext: The server's PHP lacks the zip extension.
errors.bad_zip: The .zip file is invalid or contains forbidden paths.
errors.zip_too_big: The .zip file is too large to scan.

notes.request_limit: The limit of {max} requests was reached: some checks were skipped.
notes.home_status: The home page returns HTTP {status}: the scan may be incomplete.
notes.tls_failed: The TLS certificate could not be read: {error}
notes.osv_off: The known-vulnerability check for dependencies (OSV.dev) is disabled.
notes.osv_failed: OSV.dev could not be queried ({error}): known dependency vulnerabilities are missing.
notes.max_files: The maximum of {max} files was reached: the rest were not scanned.

report.title: Stellar security report: {target}
report.intro_web: Instructions for Claude: you are a web security engineer. This is the result of an automated, non-intrusive scan of a production website that we own (or are authorized to test). There may be false positives: for each finding, first say whether you think it is real and what its impact is; then explain exactly what to change (Apache/Nginx/.htaccess configuration, PHP, the CMS or the code) with a ready-to-apply snippet. Start with the most severe. If you need to see a file or configuration to be sure, ask for it.
report.intro_code: Instructions for Claude: you are an application security engineer. This is the result of an automated static (pattern-based) analysis of the code of one of our applications. There may be false positives: for each finding, review the indicated code, say whether it is exploitable and why, and propose the concrete change (diff or corrected code) following the project's style. Start with the most severe. If you need the whole file or a function's context, ask for it.
report.none: No problems were found in the checks Stellar performs.
report.skipped: {count} findings marked as accepted, false positive or fixed are not included.
report.limits_web: The scan is external and unauthenticated: it does not test forms, private areas, business logic or active injections. Not finding a problem does not mean there is none.
report.limits_code: The analysis is pattern-based, line by line: it does not follow data across functions or files, nor review permissions, business logic or server configuration. Not finding a problem does not mean there is none.
report.ask_web:
1. A plan ordered by priority (what to do today, this week, and when possible).
2. For each real finding, the exact change to apply and how to verify it is fixed (for example, with curl).
3. The ones you think are false positives, with the reason, so we can mark them in Stellar.
report.ask_code:
1. A plan ordered by priority.
2. For each real finding, the concrete change (diff) and, if needed, a test that verifies it.
3. The ones you think are false positives, with the reason, so we can mark them in Stellar.
4. If you see other problems in the code shown, mention them.

web.no_https.title: The website has no HTTPS
web.no_https.detail: The site only works over HTTP: everything sent (passwords, forms, session cookies) travels unencrypted and can be read or modified in transit. Browsers flag it as «Not secure».
web.no_https.fix: Install a certificate (Let's Encrypt is free; on hosting panels it is usually one click), redirect all HTTP traffic to HTTPS with a 301, then enable HSTS.

web.no_https_redirect.title: HTTP does not redirect to HTTPS
web.no_https_redirect.detail: The site has HTTPS but also answers over HTTP without redirecting: anyone typing the domain or following an old link browses unencrypted.
web.no_https_redirect.fix: Redirect all HTTP to HTTPS with a 301. Apache (.htaccess): `RewriteEngine On`, `RewriteCond %{HTTPS} off`, `RewriteRule ^ https://%{HTTP_HOST}%{REQUEST_URI} [L,R=301]`. Nginx: `server { listen 80; return 301 https://$host$request_uri; }`.

web.form_http.title: Form that sends data unencrypted
web.form_http.detail: A form (or password field) is submitted over HTTP: the data travels in clear text.
web.form_http.fix: Serve the page and the form `action` over HTTPS (change `http://` to `https://` or use relative paths) and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.

web.tls_invalid.title: Invalid TLS certificate
web.tls_invalid.detail: Browsers do not trust the certificate ({error}): visitors see a security warning and encryption does not protect against impersonation.
web.tls_invalid.fix: Install a valid certificate for this domain (and www if used) from a recognised authority, with the full intermediate chain. Check with `openssl s_client -connect domain:443 -servername domain`.

web.tls_expired.title: Expired TLS certificate
web.tls_expired.detail: The certificate expired on {date}: browsers block the site with a warning.
web.tls_expired.fix: Renew the certificate now and enable automatic renewal (certbot, hosting AutoSSL…).

web.tls_expiring.title: The TLS certificate expires in {days} days
web.tls_expiring.detail: The certificate expires on {date}. If not renewed, browsers will block the site.
web.tls_expiring.fix: Check that automatic renewal works (certbot renew --dry-run, AutoSSL…) or renew it manually before {date}.

web.tls_legacy.title: Accepts {protocol}, an obsolete protocol
web.tls_legacy.detail: The server accepts {protocol}, deprecated in 2021 (RFC 8996) due to its weaknesses. No current browser needs it.
web.tls_legacy.fix: Allow only TLS 1.2 and 1.3. Apache: `SSLProtocol -all +TLSv1.2 +TLSv1.3`. Nginx: `ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;`. On shared hosting, ask the provider or change it in the panel.

web.hsts_missing.title: Missing HSTS (Strict-Transport-Security)
web.hsts_missing.detail: Without HSTS, the browser may make the first connection over HTTP and someone on the same network can intercept it before the redirect.
web.hsts_missing.fix: Add `Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` to HTTPS responses (Apache: `Header always set …` with mod_headers; Nginx: `add_header … always;`). First make sure all subdomains have HTTPS.

web.hsts_weak.title: HSTS with a short duration ({days} days)
web.hsts_weak.detail: HSTS is only remembered for {days} days; at least 6 months is recommended.

web.csp_missing.title: Missing Content Security Policy (CSP)
web.csp_missing.detail: Without Content-Security-Policy, if someone manages to inject a script (XSS) the browser runs it without any limit.
web.csp_missing.fix: Define a CSP starting in report mode (`Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`) and tune it to the domains the site uses; e.g. `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://needed-domains; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'`. When it reports no errors, switch to `Content-Security-Policy`.

web.csp_weak.title: The CSP allows dangerous scripts ({issues})
web.csp_weak.detail: The content policy allows {issues}, which cancels much of the XSS protection.
web.csp_weak.fix: Remove `'unsafe-inline'`/`'unsafe-eval'` from `script-src`: move inline scripts to files or use nonces (`'nonce-…'`) or hashes, and restrict sources to specific domains.

web.clickjacking.title: The site can be embedded in another (clickjacking)
web.clickjacking.detail: There is no X-Frame-Options nor `frame-ancestors`: another site can load this one in an invisible iframe and trick users into clicking.
web.clickjacking.fix: Add `X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN` and, in the CSP, `frame-ancestors 'self'`.

web.nosniff_missing.title: Missing X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
web.nosniff_missing.detail: Without this header the browser may interpret an uploaded file (an image, a text) as script or HTML.

web.referrer_missing.title: Missing Referrer-Policy
web.referrer_missing.detail: Without a policy, the full page address (which may carry tokens or data in parameters) is sent to linked external sites.

web.permissions_missing.title: Missing Permissions-Policy
web.permissions_missing.detail: Browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation…) available to the site and third-party iframes are not restricted.
web.permissions_missing.fix: Add e.g. `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()` (keeping only what the site needs).

web.server_version.title: The server discloses its version ({header})
web.server_version.detail: The {header} header shows «{value}»: it makes it easier to know which known vulnerabilities to try.
web.server_version.fix: Hide it. PHP: `expose_php = Off` in php.ini. Apache: `ServerTokens Prod` and `ServerSignature Off`. Nginx: `server_tokens off;`. It can also be removed with `Header unset X-Powered-By`. Above all, check that this version is still supported.

web.cookie_flags.title: Cookie «{cookie}» without {missing}
web.cookie_flags.detail: Cookie {cookie} lacks {missing}. Secure prevents sending it over HTTP; HttpOnly, reading it from a script (XSS); SameSite, sending it from other sites (CSRF).
web.cookie_flags.fix: Set it with `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` (or `Strict`). PHP: `session.cookie_secure=1`, `session.cookie_httponly=1`, `session.cookie_samesite=Lax`, or `setcookie()` options. If it comes from a plugin or external service, review its settings.

web.mixed_content.title: Mixed content: {count} resources over HTTP
web.mixed_content.detail: The page is HTTPS but loads {count} resources over HTTP. Browsers block or warn, and a script loaded this way could be modified in transit.
web.mixed_content.fix: Change those addresses to `https://` (or relative paths). In WordPress, check the site URL and search-and-replace the database. As a safety net, CSP `upgrade-insecure-requests`.

web.sri_missing.title: {count} external scripts without integrity (SRI)
web.sri_missing.detail: Scripts from other domains are loaded without the `integrity` attribute: if that server or CDN were compromised, malicious code would run on the site.
web.sri_missing.fix: Add `integrity="sha384-…" crossorigin="anonymous"` to version-pinned CDN `<script>` tags (srihash.org gives the value) or serve the files from your own domain.

web.vcs_exposed.title: Public git/svn repository ({path})
web.vcs_exposed.detail: {path} can be downloaded: automated tools rebuild the whole source code and history, including any password ever committed.
web.vcs_exposed.fix: Block access to version-control folders (Apache: `RedirectMatch 404 /\.(git|svn|hg)`; Nginx: `location ~ /\.(git|svn|hg) { deny all; }`) or, better, deploy without the .git folder. Then rotate every password and key in the history.

web.env_exposed.title: Public .env configuration file ({path})
web.env_exposed.detail: Anyone can download {path}, which usually holds database passwords, API keys and the application key.
web.env_exposed.fix: Block dot-files (Apache: `<FilesMatch "^\."> Require all denied </FilesMatch>`; Nginx: `location ~ /\. { deny all; }`) and set the document root to public/. **Rotate all credentials in it now**: consider them leaked.

web.config_backup.title: Downloadable copy of a configuration file ({path})
web.config_backup.detail: {path} is a configuration copy the server does not run as PHP and serves as text, with the database passwords.
web.config_backup.fix: Delete it from the server, block backup extensions (`.bak`, `.old`, `.save`, `~`, config `.txt`) and rotate the credentials it contained.

web.backup_exposed.title: Downloadable backup ({path})
web.backup_exposed.detail: {path} can be downloaded: a copy of the site or the database (personal data, users, passwords).
web.backup_exposed.fix: Move backups out of the public directory (outside the document root or to another service) and look for similar files. If it holds personal data, consider whether a breach notification is required (GDPR).

web.ftp_config_exposed.title: Public editor FTP/SFTP configuration ({path})
web.ftp_config_exposed.detail: {path} is the editor's upload configuration (VS Code/Sublime) and usually contains the FTP/SFTP server, user and password.
web.ftp_config_exposed.fix: Delete it from the server, add it to .gitignore and upload exclusions, and change the FTP/SFTP password.

web.htpasswd_exposed.title: Public .htpasswd file
web.htpasswd_exposed.detail: The users and hashed passwords of the protected area can be downloaded; weak ones can be cracked.
web.htpasswd_exposed.fix: Move .htpasswd outside the document root (or block `^\.ht`) and change the passwords.

web.adminer_exposed.title: Adminer reachable ({path})
web.adminer_exposed.detail: A database manager is exposed: a common brute-force target that has had serious vulnerabilities.
web.adminer_exposed.fix: Delete it when not in use or protect it with another layer (allowed IPs, HTTP password).

web.phpinfo_exposed.title: Public phpinfo() page ({path})
web.phpinfo_exposed.detail: {path} shows the full PHP and server configuration: paths, versions, modules and sometimes environment variables with secrets.

web.log_exposed.title: Public log file ({path})
web.log_exposed.detail: {path} is a downloadable error log: it reveals server paths, queries, versions and sometimes user data.
web.log_exposed.fix: Delete it, store logs outside the document root (WordPress: `WP_DEBUG_LOG` with a private path, or `WP_DEBUG` false in production) and block `*.log`.

web.server_status.title: Public Apache server status (/server-status)
web.server_status.detail: It shows live requests to the server, with URLs, visitor IPs and parameters.
web.server_status.fix: Restrict `/server-status` to localhost (`Require local`) or disable mod_status.

web.phpmyadmin_exposed.title: phpMyAdmin reachable ({path})
web.phpmyadmin_exposed.detail: Exposed phpMyAdmin is a common target for brute force and vulnerabilities.
web.phpmyadmin_exposed.fix: Remove it from the public site or restrict it by IP / with a second HTTP password.

web.debug_mode.title: Debug tool in production ({path})
web.debug_mode.detail: {path} is a development tool (profiler or debug panel) that shows requests, queries, variables and sometimes secrets.
web.debug_mode.fix: Disable development mode in production (Symfony: `APP_ENV=prod`; Laravel: `APP_DEBUG=false` and Telescope only locally).

web.junk_files.title: Developer machine files published ({path})
web.junk_files.detail: {path} reveals internal file and folder names of the project.
web.junk_files.fix: Delete them and add them to .gitignore and upload exclusions.

web.dir_listing.title: Directory listing of {path} visible
web.dir_listing.detail: The server lists every file in {path}: anyone can see and download documents that are not linked.
web.dir_listing.fix: Disable listings: Apache `Options -Indexes` (in .htaccess); Nginx `autoindex off;`. Review what is in the folder.

web.cors_reflect.title: CORS accepts any origin (credentials: {credentials})
web.cors_reflect.detail: The server answers any external site with Access-Control-Allow-Origin equal to its origin (Allow-Credentials: {credentials}). If «true», a malicious site can read user data with their session.
web.cors_reflect.fix: Only answer origins from a specific allow-list and never use `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true` with non-fixed origins.

web.reflected_input.title: The site echoes URL input unescaped (possible XSS)
web.reflected_input.detail: A parameter with quotes and `<` was returned as-is inside the HTML. Very likely a reflected XSS: a crafted link can run code in the browser of whoever opens it.
web.reflected_input.fix: Always escape output for its context (`htmlspecialchars($value, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8')` in PHP, `esc_html()`/`esc_attr()` in WordPress) and add a CSP. Find where the parameter is used in the code.

web.error_disclosure.title: Internal error messages visible ({kind})
web.error_disclosure.detail: The site shows internal errors ({kind}) to visitors: paths, SQL queries or traces that help attackers and may indicate an injection.
web.error_disclosure.fix: In production, `display_errors = Off` and `log_errors = On` (log outside the web root); disable framework debug mode. If it is an SQL error triggered by the quotes, review the query: it probably does not use prepared statements.

web.trace_enabled.title: TRACE method enabled
web.trace_enabled.detail: The server answers TRACE by echoing the request, which combined with other flaws can be used to steal cookies (XST).
web.trace_enabled.fix: Apache: `TraceEnable Off`. Nginx does not support it by default; check the proxy.

web.cms_version.title: {cms} version visible ({version})
web.cms_version.detail: The site says it uses {cms} {version}. If it is not the latest, it has known public vulnerabilities.
web.cms_version.fix: Update {cms} to the latest version (and plugins/themes) and hide the version (WordPress: remove the meta generator and readme.html).

web.wp_plugins.title: WordPress plugins detected ({count})
web.wp_plugins.fix: Check that all are up to date and free of known vulnerabilities (wpscan.com/plugins, patchstack.com/database) and remove unused ones.

web.wp_xmlrpc.title: WordPress XML-RPC enabled
web.wp_xmlrpc.detail: xmlrpc.php accepts requests: it allows trying many passwords in a single request (system.multicall) and pingback attacks.
web.wp_xmlrpc.fix: If unused (Jetpack, mobile app), disable it: plugin, filter `add_filter('xmlrpc_enabled', '__return_false');` or block `xmlrpc.php` on the server.

web.wp_user_enum.title: WordPress users can be listed
web.wp_user_enum.detail: The REST API shows usernames ({users}): half of the credentials for a brute-force attack.
web.wp_user_enum.fix: Restrict `/wp-json/wp/v2/users` to logged-in users (`rest_endpoints` filter or a security plugin), block `?author=N`, and enable login rate limiting and 2FA.

web.security_txt.title: Missing security.txt
web.security_txt.detail: There is no /.well-known/security.txt, the standard file (RFC 9116) telling vulnerability finders whom to contact.
web.security_txt.fix: Publish `/.well-known/security.txt` with at least `Contact: mailto:security@…` and `Expires: …`.

web.robots_paths.title: robots.txt points to sensitive paths
web.robots_paths.detail: robots.txt lists paths that look private ({paths}). It protects nothing: it only advertises them.
web.robots_paths.fix: Do not list private paths in robots.txt; protect them with authentication.

web.js_vulnerable.title: {package} {version} has {count} known vulnerabilities
web.js_vulnerable.detail: The site loads the JavaScript library {package} {version}, with {count} published vulnerabilities (see evidence).
web.js_vulnerable.fix: Update {package} to at least {fixed} (ideally the latest stable) and check the site still works. If the theme or a plugin bundles it, update that.

code.sqli.title: Possible SQL injection in {file}
code.sqli.detail: SQL queries are built by concatenating variables ({count} lines). If any comes from the user unvalidated, the whole database can be read or modified.
code.sqli.fix: Use prepared statements with parameters (`?` or `:name`) for every value; for column names or ordering, an allow-list. Escaping is not enough.

code.cmd_injection.title: Possible OS command execution in {file}
code.cmd_injection.detail: System commands run with variables ({count} lines). If any comes from the user, anything can be executed on the server.
code.cmd_injection.fix: Avoid the shell: use language functions or pass arguments as a list (proc_open with an array, `spawn` without `shell`, `subprocess.run([...])`). If unavoidable, `escapeshellarg()` on every argument plus an allow-list.

code.file_inclusion.title: Include/require with user data in {file}
code.file_inclusion.detail: A PHP file is loaded using a name from the request: it can allow code execution or reading server files.
code.file_inclusion.fix: Never include paths that come from the user: use an allow-list (`match`/array of allowed values → file).

code.path_traversal.title: File access with user-supplied paths in {file}
code.path_traversal.detail: Files are opened, read or deleted with a path from the request ({count} lines): with `../` any file can be reached.
code.path_traversal.fix: Use identifiers instead of paths, or `basename()` + `realpath()` and check the result is inside the allowed folder.

code.unserialize.title: Unsafe deserialization in {file}
code.unserialize.detail: Data is deserialized ({count} lines) with `unserialize`/`pickle`/`yaml.load`. With attacker data this can end in code execution.
code.unserialize.fix: Use JSON (`json_decode`, `json.loads`). If PHP unserialize is needed, `['allowed_classes' => false]`; in Python, `yaml.safe_load`.

code.eval.title: Use of eval or equivalent in {file}
code.eval.detail: Code built at runtime is executed ({count} lines). If any external data gets in, it is remote code execution.
code.eval.fix: Rewrite it without eval (function maps, JSON.parse, etc.).

code.xss.title: Possible XSS: unescaped output in {file}
code.xss.detail: Data is printed without escaping ({count} lines), in some cases straight from the request. It can allow running scripts in other users' browsers.
code.xss.fix: Escape for the context: PHP `htmlspecialchars($v, ENT_QUOTES, 'UTF-8')` (or `esc_html`/`esc_attr` in WordPress); JavaScript `textContent` instead of `innerHTML`, or DOMPurify if HTML is needed.

code.open_redirect.title: Open redirect in {file}
code.open_redirect.detail: It redirects to an address from the request: usable for phishing links that look like your site.
code.open_redirect.fix: Only redirect to internal paths (starting with `/` but not `//`) or to an allow-list of domains (`wp_safe_redirect` in WordPress).

code.mass_assignment.title: extract()/parse_str() with request data in {file}
code.mass_assignment.detail: Request parameters become variables: an attacker can overwrite any variable (permissions, paths…).
code.mass_assignment.fix: Read only the fields you need, explicitly (`$_POST['name'] ?? ''`).

code.weak_password_hash.title: Passwords hashed weakly in {file}
code.weak_password_hash.detail: MD5/SHA1/SHA256 is used for passwords: after a leak they are cracked in minutes.
code.weak_password_hash.fix: Use `password_hash()` / `password_verify()` (bcrypt or Argon2) and migrate old hashes at next login.

code.upload.title: File upload keeps the original name in {file}
code.upload.detail: The uploaded file is saved with the user-supplied name: a `.php` could be uploaded and executed, or files overwritten.
code.upload.fix: Generate the name yourself (random), validate extension and real type (finfo) against an allow-list, and store it outside the document root or in a folder without PHP execution.

code.weak_random.title: Insecure randomness for tokens in {file}
code.weak_random.detail: Tokens, passwords or codes are generated with `rand`/`mt_rand`/`uniqid`/`Math.random`, which are predictable.

code.loose_compare.title: Non-strict comparison of tokens or hashes in {file}
code.loose_compare.detail: Tokens, hashes or passwords are compared with `==`: PHP type juggling can make different values look equal, and timing can leak the value.
code.loose_compare.fix: Use `hash_equals()` for tokens and hashes and `password_verify()` for passwords.

code.prototype_pollution.title: Possible prototype pollution in {file}
code.prototype_pollution.detail: Properties are assigned with keys from the request: with `__proto__` every object in the app can be altered.

code.debug_enabled.title: Debug mode enabled in {file}
code.debug_enabled.detail: The configuration displays errors or enables debug mode: in production it reveals internal information.
code.debug_enabled.fix: Disable it in production (make it environment-dependent): `display_errors=Off`, `APP_DEBUG=false`, `DEBUG=False`.

code.tls_verify_off.title: HTTPS connections without certificate verification in {file}
code.tls_verify_off.detail: Certificate verification is disabled ({count} lines): anyone can impersonate the remote server and read or alter the data (API keys included).
code.tls_verify_off.fix: Remove the options that disable verification; if the issue was the certificate chain, configure the CA file (`CURLOPT_CAINFO`) instead.

code.cors_any.title: CORS open to any origin in {file}
code.cors_any.detail: It answers `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`: any site can read these responses from users' browsers.
code.cors_any.fix: If the API is public with no private data this may be fine; otherwise restrict it to a list of origins.

code.secret.title: Key or token ({kind}) hardcoded in {file}
code.secret.detail: There is a real credential ({kind}) in the code. Anyone with access to the code or repository (or a leaked copy) can use it.
code.secret.fix: Revoke it and create a new one **now**, move it to an environment variable or a config file outside the repository (like `config.local.php` or a git-ignored `.env`) and, if it is in a repository, purge it from history (git filter-repo).

code.hardcoded_credential.title: Password or key hardcoded in {file}
code.hardcoded_credential.detail: Credentials are written directly in the code ({count} lines).
code.hardcoded_credential.fix: Move them to configuration outside the repository (environment variables, git-ignored `config.local.php` or `.env`) and rotate them if the code has been shared.

code.env_file.title: Secrets file inside the project ({file})
code.env_file.detail: {file} contains passwords or keys and is part of the delivered code (if it is in git, they stay in the history).
code.env_file.fix: Remove it from the repository (`git rm --cached`), add it to .gitignore, keep a `.env.example` without values and rotate the credentials if the repository was shared.

code.dep_vulnerable.title: Vulnerable dependency: {package} {version}
code.dep_vulnerable.fix: Update {package} to at least {fixed} (`composer update {package}` / `npm install {package}@latest` / `pip install -U {package}`), run the tests and scan again.
